newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX vols aloft as dollar ratchets higher.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX vols aloft as dollar ratchets higher.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar-pair options were firmer at U.S. midsession as the spot greenback extended recent gains to reach fresh multi-year highs, dealers said.
Given the dollar's quick advances in the past several days on top of already hefty gains so far this year, shorter-dated volatilities were particularly well bid, they added.
"Certainly no one is going to look to having any kind of a short-gamma position here," Alan Revercomb, options strategist at I.D.E.A. Inc, said.
Shorter-dated options have higher gamma values, meaning short positions in them would make big losses on a big move in spot rates but benefit from time-decay in a stable market.

"We have got actual volatility in dollar/mark that has moved up to a point to justify these levels (in implied volatilities)," Revercomb said. "I think the market both analytically and intuitively feels that it pays to be long gamma and even more so to have a directional bias."
He said a daily movement of a pfennig in dollar/mark equated to about 9.6 percent in one-month actual volatility and that such a swing had lately been easily attainable.
Implied volatility for one-month dollar/mark options was quoted at around 9.8/10.1 percent in late morning U.S. business, up from 9.1/9.3 late on Tuesday.
Earlier in the day, the dollar rose to a 31-month high of 1.6455 marks, about 1.5 pfennigs above late Tuesday levels.
The dollar also rose to 119.20 yen, a 46-month high. One-month dollar/yen implied volatility stood at 9.6/9.9 percent, up from Tuesday's 8.9/9.2 percent.
With spot tirelessly shifting its trading range higher, many formerly out-of-the-money options were quickly gaining delta, putting a squeeze on option writers, traders said.
Delta represents the rate at which premiums change per move in the spot rate.
The dollar has also been penetrating various exotic option barrier prices, or threatening to do so, adding fuel to the bid-tone in volatilities, a Japanese bank trader added.
"Unless the BOJ (Bank of Japan) starts to intervene, 120 yen is within reach," he said.

Risk reversals, which reflect pricing differential of puts and calls, widened their skew for dollar calls. One-month 25-delta stood at 0.4/0.8 percent bid for mark puts and 0.0/0.3 percent bid in favor of yen puts.
With the market's perception becoming so unidirectional, some traders warned of an eventual pullback.
Revercomb said dollar/yen volatilities could be the most vulnerable, with spot approaching the 120 yen resistance.
But a pullback in dollar/mark would be a buying opportunity, given the fundamentals strongly suggesting a continued long-term bullish trend, he said.
"Everybody's waited for a pullback and it hasn't really come in spot, it hasn't really come in vols," he noted. If you get a half-figure (half-pfennig), one-figure pullback, you've got to buy."
